text: Collaborative Calls for Proposals Home Agreements Collaborative Calls for Proposals Joint Call for Proposals of the PROASA-FAPESP Program and Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo (ANID) 2025 Versão em português Page updated on 07/23/2025 - Published on 06/12/2025 Call announcement: July 23, 2025 Deadline for submission: September 1, 2025 Selection results announcement: December, 2025 Start of projects: December, 2025 FAPESP Support Modality: Regular Research Grant Eligibility: Researchers affiliated with Higher Education or Research Institutions in the state of São Paulo and Researchers from Chile Submission: Only to FAPESP via SAGe (www.fapesp.br/sage) FAPESP Contact Details: chamada-proasa-anid@fapesp.br ANID Contact Details: https://ayuda.anid.cl/ Funding Opportunity Announcement at ANID: https://anid.cl/calendario-concursos-2025/ 1. Introduction The FAPESP Program for the South Atlantic Ocean and Antarctica (PROASA) aims to contribute to the generation, dissemination, and application of knowledge through scientific, technological, and innovative approaches in two interconnected and still underexplored systems: the South Atlantic Ocean and Antarctica. These systems modulate processes that both positively and negatively influence the potential for sustainable development in the state of São Paulo, in Brazil, and globally. PROASA focuses on research related to coastal areas and marine environments in the South Atlantic—within and beyond national jurisdiction—and in Antarctica, which includes the Antarctic continent and the Southern Ocean (also known as the Antarctic Ocean). The new Call for Proposals under the PROASA-FAPESP Program is being launched within the framework of the ongoing collaboration, since 2016, with Chile’s Agencia Nacional de Investigación y Desarrollo (ANID). This initiative represents a significant step forward in the continuation of this bilateral alliance and reinforces the commitment of both agencies to joint development in science, technology, and innovation, as well as to the exchange of human capital. Projects, all scheduled to begin in January 2026, must have a duration of up to 36 months (3 years) and be equivalent on both sides. Researchers from the state of São Paulo interested in submitting proposals to this Call must follow the guidelines described in the Regular Research Grant program, with exceptions regarding budget allocation as outlined in this call. Chilean researchers must follow ANID's guidelines, available at https://anid.cl/calendario-concursos-2025/. 2. Research Areas Scientific cooperation proposals will be accepted if they are explicitly connected to the South Atlantic Ocean and/or Antarctica and address themes such as biodiversity, oceanic processes, latitudinal studies, governance, and other human dimensions, as exemplified by the topics addressed within the PROASA program (PROASA). Only one proposal per Principal Investigator (PI) may be submitted under this Call. 3. Eligibility of Researchers The eligibility of the PIs will be assessed by FAPESP and ANID after the submission of proposals. Only proposals deemed eligible will proceed to the merit review stage. 3.1. Eligible researchers for FAPESP: Researchers eligible for FAPESP funding under the scope of this Call must be employees of public or private Higher Education or Research Institutions in the state of São Paulo and must meet the FAPESP eligibility requirements for Auxílio à Pesquisa Regular. 3.2. Eligible researchers for ANID: At ANID, PIs submitting a proposal must also send the following documents through the platform https://ayuda.anid.cl, for review: • Completed budget annex, using the format provided by ANID, in English; • Letter of commitment to the project, signed by the Principal Investigator (PI) from the São Paulo team; • Letter of commitment from the Chilean institution, duly signed by its legal representative or a delegated authority, in accordance with the format provided by ANID; • Document verifying the legal nature of the beneficiary institution, such as the institution's bylaws, articles of incorporation, or a similar official document. To submit a proposal under this Call, the PI and the co-PI from Chile must be affiliated with the same institution. 4. Funding Modality and Eligible Costs 4.1. Eligible Costs for FAPESP: FAPESP will cover the research team costs on the São Paulo side. Funding and eligible expenses must comply with the rules outlined under Auxílio à Pesquisa Regular. Exceptionally for this Call, in addition to the fellowships normally allowed under this funding line, an additional Postdoctoral Fellowship might be requested, which will not be counted toward the maximum total grant amount of BRL 600,000 for the three-year period. 4.2. Eligible Costs for ANID: ANID will cover the research team costs on the Chilean side. Funding and eligible expenses include personnel costs and operational expenses, as described in https://anid.cl/calendario-concursos-2025/. 5. Proposal Submission 5.1 Each proposal must have one PI based in the state of São Paulo and one based in Chile. Each PI may submit only one proposal under this Call. 5.2 The research project must be jointly designed and written by the proponents from São Paulo and Chile, and submitted as a single version in English. In addition to the documents required in SAGe, a budget spreadsheet must be included, containing the amounts requested by the São Paulo team from FAPESP and by the Chilean team from ANID. 5.3 Proposals must be submitted exclusively to FAPESP by the PI from São Paulo through the SAGe system (www.fapesp.br/sage). • The specific path in the SAGe system for this Call is: Nova Proposta Inicial > + Outras Linhas de Fomento > + Programas de Inovação Tecnológica > + PROASA - Program for the South Atlantic Ocean and Antarctic sciences > + PROASA - Projeto de Pesquisa – Regular > Chamada de Propostas (2025) ANID • Please bear in mind that: • The PI from the United Kingdom and all co-PIs from the state of São Paulo must be registered in the SAGe system and confirm their participation in the proposal. • Researchers who do not have a SAGe registration must initially do so by accessing the SAGe page at www.fapesp.br/sage, clicking No registration? and filling in the requested data. It is not enough to just register as a user. After accessing the system it is necessary to complete the mandatory registration data, marqued with “*”. • Researchers already registered must login to SAGe with their usual identification and password to access the system. • When submitting the proposal, pay attention to the mandatory completion of all items marked with *. It is necessary to submit the proposal at the end. A saved proposal does not mean that it is a submitted proposal. • In case of doubts, on the SAGe home page there is a link to the Manuals that can be used and, on the Manuals page, seek clarifications in the list Manuals de Apoio aos Pesquisadores. The system also provides an English version with manuals for user registration and confirmation of participation in proposals. IMPORTANT: It is strongly recommended to complete and submit the proposal in the system well in advance and that the researcher periodically checks the pending proposals using the "Validate" option in SAGe. This can be done repeatedly as the proposal is constructed, allowing all necessary arrangements for submission to be made on time. When selecting the “Validate” option, the SAGe system will present the pending issues that impede the submission of the proposal considering the items that were inserted. In case of doubts about the use of SAGe, in addition to the Manuals, FAPESP also provides assistance through the Converse with FAPESP service at converse. 5.4 The submission deadline for proposals is September 1, 2025. 5.5 No proposals will be accepted after the submission deadline. Likewise, no addenda or clarifications will be accepted, unless explicitly and formally requested by FAPESP or ANID. Incomplete proposals will not be reviewed. 6. Evaluation and Selection FAPESP will act as the Lead Agency for the evaluation of proposals submitted under this Call. • A Joint Steering Committee will be established, composed of subject-matter experts selected by the PROASA Program at FAPESP and by ANID. • This Committee will conduct an initial screening to verify whether proposals comply with the rules of this Call. Proposals that do not meet the requirements outlined in this Call for Proposals will not proceed to merit review. • Proposals deemed eligible will be sent for peer review by at least two external experts, appointed by the Steering Committee. • Upon receipt of the external reviews, the proposals will be evaluated by a Review Panel composed of members of the Steering Committee and other invited experts. Based on the assessment criteria described in the funding modality for this Call, the Panel will prioritize the proposals recommended for funding. • The results of the Review Panel will be analyzed by the respective Scientific or Technical Councils of FAPESP and ANID. The final results will then be communicated first via email to the applicants and subsequently published on the official websites of the respective agencies. 7. Intellectual Property In case of approval of the proposal, a Letter of Agreement (or “Consortium Agreement”) must be signed between the partner Host Institutions (from the United Kingdom and from the state of São Paulo), establishing how Intellectual Property rights, confidentiality, publications and data sharing will be treated jointly, in accordance to the policies of each Funding Agency and each Host Institution. Note that no specific format for this agreement will be provided by ANID or FAPESP. Presentation of this document is not mandatory for signing the Grant Term. However, the two agencies can request this document any time. 8. Matchmaking Chilean researchers interested in finding partners in the state of São Paulo can use the Virtual Library of FAPESP, which provides an interface to get in touch with researchers funded by FAPESP by sending them a message. It is possible to search for information regarding Grants and Scholarships awarded by FAPESP, including abstracts, as well as the names of participating researchers and their institutions. 9. Benefits and Commitments of Joining PROASA 9.1 Benefits of joining PROASA: • Broad opportunities for interaction with other researchers through thematic workshops, meetings, and participation in working groups organized by the program’s coordination team; • Increased visibility of scientific activities, supported by FAPESP through its communication strategy and tools. 9.2 Commitments of Joining PROASA: • Researchers with projects affiliated with PROASA must submit the program’s monitoring form along with the project's annual report, using the form available on PROASA; • Researchers with projects under PROASA commit to managing the data produced in accordance with the submitted Data Management Plan, aligned with FAPESP’s Data Management Policy (Gestão de dados).
